acceptance.given: Atomic Obligations and runtime-evidence links are assembled for evaluation.

oracle.expected: Validation artifact reports a one-to-one reciprocal mapping covering every Atomic Obligation and every runtime-evidence node with no missing or orphan links.
forbidden: Any Atomic Obligation lacks runtime-evidence coverage.
Any runtime-evidence link is one-directional or orphaned.
oracle.observable: The conformance validator's coverage report contains complete reciprocal obligation-to-runtime-evidence and runtime-evidence-to-obligation mappings.

acceptance.then: The validator emits an exact reciprocal runtime-evidence coverage result for every Atomic Obligation.
acceptance.when: During conformance validation, inspect the generated Exact Cover relation in the validation phase.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Remove or invert one runtime-evidence edge and run the conformance validator; the missing or orphan mapping must be detected.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Add or preserve validator checks that prove bidirectional Exact Cover for runtime evidence, rejecting missing, one-way, and orphan links.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Keep existing conformance input and report schemas backward compatible; rollback only validator logic.

slice_hint.state_transition: Unverified runtime-evidence coverage becomes validated reciprocal Exact Cover.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Validator output contains reciprocal coverage for every Atomic Obligation and runtime-evidence node with zero missing or orphan edges.

acceptance.given: An infrastructure-failure Probe outcome is classified as a false negative during evaluation.

oracle.expected: Evaluation result is failed and explicitly identifies the infrastructure-failure false-negative case.
forbidden: The false negative is accepted without a failure verdict.
oracle.observable: The evaluation result record contains a failed verdict for the infrastructure-failure false-negative case.

acceptance.then: The evaluator marks the infrastructure-failure false-negative case as failed.
acceptance.when: Execute the evaluator against a detached Probe result representing an infrastructure failure that was incorrectly reported as success.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run the evaluator with an infrastructure-failure Probe forced to report success; the evaluation must return a failure verdict.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Ensure infrastructure-failure false negatives are classified and fail evaluation rather than being treated as successful Probe outcomes.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve existing runtime-evidence schema and verdict fields; rollback classification logic only.

slice_hint.state_transition: Infrastructure-failure false-negative input becomes an explicit failed evaluation verdict.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: A forced infrastructure-failure false-negative produces a failed evaluation result and never a pass.

acceptance.given: A Replay Result has reached a successful status and includes output data.

oracle.expected: The successful Replay Result contains an independently produced verification record for the output, distinct from the output claim itself.
forbidden: Success is asserted without an independent output verification.
The verification merely aliases the unverified output claim.
oracle.observable: Replay Result artifact exposes a separate output-verification field or record whose provenance is independently checked.

acceptance.then: Validation accepts the Replay Result only when independent output verification is present and consistent.
acceptance.when: Inspect and validate a successful Replay Result artifact in the replay-result validation phase.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Delete or alias the independent output-verification record in an otherwise successful Replay Result and validate the artifact; validation must fail.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Require successful Replay Result artifacts to carry independently verifiable output evidence rather than trusting the output claim alone.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Retain existing Replay Result artifact structure; add only mandatory independent-verification validation.

slice_hint.state_transition: Successful Replay Result moves from output-claimed to independently output-verified.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Package validation rejects any successful Replay Result lacking a distinct independently verified output record.

acceptance.given: The FR-10 enable/disable/rollback/re-enable flow is executed for each applicable Consumer.

oracle.expected: Each applicable Consumer has a recorded completed disable operation invoked through its real repository call surface.
forbidden: Disable is performed only through a simulated, indirect, or nonexistent call surface.
Any applicable Consumer lacks a completed disable record.
oracle.observable: The execution record maps every applicable Consumer to a concrete repository caller and a completed disable operation.

acceptance.then: Validation confirms a real call-surface disable completion for every applicable Consumer.
acceptance.when: During FR-10 route-flow execution, inspect the call-surface execution records for each Consumer.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Substitute a simulated or missing disable caller for one applicable Consumer and validate the FR-10 execution records; validation must fail.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Record and validate disable operations through concrete repository call surfaces for every applicable Consumer in the FR-10 flow.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve existing route and Consumer record formats; rollback call-surface validation changes only.

slice_hint.state_transition: Consumer disable state changes from pending to completed through a recorded real caller.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Every applicable Consumer has a completed disable record bound to a concrete repository call surface, with no simulated-only entry.
